name: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
aliases: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of small to medium-sized pleomorphic CD4+ T-cells with epidermotropism and dermal infiltration
Immunohistochemistry showing CD3+, CD4+, CD8-, CD30- phenotype
Solitary or localized erythematous to violaceous plaques or nodules primarily on the head, neck, or upper trunk
Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement detected by PCR
No evidence of extracutaneous disease on staging workup

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of characteristic CD4+ pleomorphic T-cell infiltrate with appropriate immunophenotype and absence of systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary or localized erythematous to violaceous cutaneous plaques or nodules
searchTerms: single or few red-purple skin plaques

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dermal infiltration by small to medium-sized pleomorphic CD4+ T-cells
searchTerms: small to medium abnormal T-cells in skin
pruritus limited to affected skin areas

common.symptomName: Slowly progressive cutaneous lesions over months to years
Absence of systemic B symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats)

occasional.symptomName: Mild localized pain or tenderness at lesion site
searchTerms: mild pain or tenderness at lesion

rare.notes: Very rare in primary cutaneous form

searchTerms: skin lesions that disappear on their own

laboratory: Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement by PCR
Absence of systemic inflammatory markers elevation
imaging: Negative PET/CT or CT scans for extracutaneous disease
No lymphadenopathy or organomegaly on imaging
other: Histopathology showing dermal infiltrate of pleomorphic CD4+ T-cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3 and CD4, negative for CD8 and CD30

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly CD4+ but with larger atypical cells
Patch and plaque stages with epidermotropism

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or ulcerating skin lesions
Evidence of systemic symptoms such as unexplained fever or weight loss
Detection of extracutaneous disease on imaging or biopsy
references: Willemze R, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC. 2017.
Bekkenk MW, et al. Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma: clinical and pathological features. J Cutan Pathol. 2000.
